_comment: Each people's arts (Dwarf Fortress style, two layers): a vocabulary made once per people from these tables (instruments, poetic, musical and dance forms, biased by race), then each form credited to a real figure of that people, in a real year and town. Words in {braces} are filled: {instrument}, {subject}, {lines}, {people}.

instruments._comment: Kinds of instrument: [kind, how it is played, the materials it may be made of].

subjects._comment: What a work is about, by the culture's leaning.

poetic: a lament of {lines}-line stanzas, each ending on the name of the dead, about {subject}
a boast spoken by one voice and answered by many, about {subject}
a riddle-poem of {lines} lines whose answer is never said aloud, about {subject}
a chant in which every line repeats the last word of the one before, about {subject}
a long saga in lines of {lines} beats, told over many nights, about {subject}
a short verse of {lines} lines with the same sound at the end of each, about {subject}
musical: a slow air for the {instrument}, played at burials
a marching tune for the {instrument} and many voices
a work song for the {instrument}, kept in time by those who labour
a round sung in {lines} parts over the {instrument}
a wild piece for the {instrument} that quickens until the players stop
a cradle song sung softly over the {instrument}
dance: a circle dance around a fire, faster at each turn
a line dance of stamping feet and clapping hands
a war dance of {lines} dancers with spears
a slow dance of pairs that turn and part
a leaping dance done by the young at the turn of the year
